correctness.rationale: For arbitrary regular conditional CDFs, d(u,v)=F_{V|U=u}(v)−v is L². Independent reflection sends d(u,v) to −d(u,1−v). Its antisymmetric and symmetric pieces E and O are orthogonal. W_p has centered conditional CDF E+(2p−1)O, hence xi(W_p|U)=6||E||²+6(2p−1)²||O||². The fold T is uniform and its conditional-centered CDF is 2E(u,t/2); symmetry/change of variables yield xi(T|U)=24||E||². These exact identities prove the claimed attenuation and all boundary p=0,1/2,1 cases. Total variance characterizes xi=1 (response measurable from predictor) and xi=0 (independence). The explicit mixture V=U with probability a or independent U′ otherwise gives xi(V|U)=xi(T|U)=a², attaining every exact capacity value a²[1−3p(1−p)]. Reflective symmetry forces tau=rho=0 at p=1/2. The current embedded checker verify.py passed 2752 exact Fraction checks; these finite calculations do not establish universal claims.

value.rationale: Random loss of response orientation is a natural dependence-measurement channel. The all-copula exact transition law quantifies its degradation for every probability, reveals a folded-information invariant, and completely classifies attainable capacity and both upper/zero equality conditions. In particular, the fair channel preserves up to xi=1/4 while removing Kendall/Spearman concordance, so the result distinguishes directed predictability from sign-sensitive association. The theorem goes beyond a known endpoint example by classifying an entire class of randomization channels with a structural proof; no general downstream theorem is needed.
